pros: Optimal linear time complexity: O(V + E) — provably optimal
Hierarchical nested structure reveals core-periphery organization
More robust than degree centrality (considers global context)
Better predictor of spreading influence than degree (Kitsak et al., 2010)
Extremely efficient on large-scale graphs (billions of edges)
Simple to implement with clear algorithm (bucket sort + peeling)
Provides upper bound for chromatic number (χ ≤ degeneracy + 1)
Applicable to both directed and undirected graphs
Stable: small edge changes typically affect only nearby cores
cons: Cannot distinguish nodes with same core number
Insensitive to edge weights in the basic version
Does not capture community structure directly
High-degree low-core nodes may be counterintuitive
Single peeling order may not reflect all structural nuances
Cannot handle signed or negative edge weights naturally
Limited to static graphs (requires recomputation for updates)
K-core may be disconnected (not a single connected component)
Does not consider path lengths or betweenness
May be too coarse for very homogeneous graphs
Core number of 0 for isolated nodes may not be meaningful
